source: Can you make a pet game where you open eggs and you break lucky blocks that give you money that make it so you can buy more pits and can you make it so these 12 areas and can you make it so to get to the areas you have to have unlocked a certain amount of pet

answers.ask: Should the areas be bright and cartoony, or does each of the twelve have its own look?
answers.answer: Make the game bright and cartoony, with each of the 12 areas having its own simple look.

answers.ask: How big is each area - a small yard, or somewhere you spend minutes walking?
answers.answer: Make each area a small yard-sized zone so players can quickly find lucky blocks, eggs, and the next area.

answers.ask: How many pets does each of the twelve areas need before it opens?
answers.answer: Each new area should require more pets than the last, starting at 1 pet for area 2 and increasing by 1 pet per area up to 11 pets for area 12.

config.genre_evidence: The core layout is an incremental pet-collection loop: players "open eggs," "break lucky blocks that give you money," use money to "buy more pets," and unlock twelve small zones by owning increasing numbers of pets. The gated areas add a light Adventure progression layer, but the space is primarily built around collecting, earning, and upgrading pets.

config.addendum:
LAYOUT FEATURES for this Simulation map. Build these as the actual structure of the space rather than as set dressing, keep them visually distinct from one another, and keep the whole layout legible in one view.

SHAPE OF THE SPACE - Shared Persistent World: No personal plot at all — one common world everybody operates in together.

INCLUDE:
- Upgrades Bazaar: The central storefront zone — eggs, upgrades, progression shops — that every player has to keep coming back to.
- Purchase Gate: Physical walls blocking higher-tier zones that animate away, drop into the ground, or vanish when bought.
- Progression Circulation: Walkable or drivable circulation chaining the hub to wherever value is actually produced.
